llm.summary: This document-conversion skill is purpose-aligned, but normal use can install packages, modify local tool environments, and overwrite files without enough separate user control.

dimensions.detail: Local document parsing, LibreOffice/Office preprocessing, and Markdown output are proportionate to the purpose. However, support for YouTube/transcription-related extras and automatic registry access is not cleanly separated from local-only conversion expectations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: QUICKSTART.md recommends a pipe-to-shell uv installer, and convert.py can run pip install plus uv tool install --force during normal conversion. The packages are named, but versions and integrity checks are not pinned or verified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions disclose several confirmation points for batch traversal and output overwrites, but dependency installation is framed as automatic and zero-intervention. That leaves users without a clear opt-in before network package retrieval and environment mutation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Expected outputs and _conversion_errors.log persist, which conflicts with the SKILL.md claim that no traceable artifacts remain. post_clean.py also overwrites its input by default and deletes its backup after writing, and automatic package installs persist in the host environment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose is coherent: convert local documents to Markdown, clean the output, handle legacy Office formats, and support batch conversion. The subprocess converters and file reads/writes fit that purpose, but the capability set is broad for a document skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing in a sensitive environment. Use it only where automatic package installation from PyPI/uv is acceptable, avoid untrusted documents unless conversion is sandboxed, confirm batch scopes and output paths carefully, and prefer explicit output paths for post_clean.py so originals are not overwritten.
llm.findings:
[AST4] expected: Subprocess use for markitdown, uvx, pip, and LibreOffice is expected for this converter. The material concern is the automatic package installation and forced uv tool install during normal use, not the mere existence of subprocess calls.
[LP3] expected: The artifact discloses shell, filesystem, platform detection, and package-management behavior in documentation, but the metadata only declares required binaries and does not provide a narrower permission scope.
[SDI-4] expected: Persistent Markdown outputs and batch error logs are expected for conversion, but the privacy statement overstates cleanup by claiming no traceable artifacts remain.
[SDI-2] expected: Dependency installation supports the stated conversion workflow, but fetching and installing unpinned packages from registries at runtime expands the trust boundary and persists changes without a distinct approval step.
[SQP-2] expected: The README and QUICKSTART disclose automatic dependency installation, yet the remote installer guidance, runtime installs, network-capable extras, and default in-place post-clean behavior create real review concerns for supply-chain and recoverability risk.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrases are broad but still centered on document-to-Markdown conversion. This is a lesser concern by itself because the SKILL.md includes confirmation requirements for batch traversal and overwrites.
